retainedReference.title: Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus
retainedReference.description: The poliadic temple of the ancient city of Rome
retainedReference.reason: No unique physical footprint or centerline with exact Wikidata identity has been resolved.

pictures.author: Joris
pictures.observations: Actually inspected the full photograph: long grey tufa foundation face, many large offset courses, broad broken upper edge, parallel lower masonry and modern museum walls with spiral stairs. No complete ancient colonnade or roof survives in this view.

pictures.author: Torquatus
pictures.observations: Actually inspected the full photograph: massive rectangular cappellaccio blocks, recessed joints, stepped broken top and a broad lower surviving mass inside modern white museum walls. Individual block lengths, depth and upper profile are approximate photographic interpretations.

pictures.author: Horcrux
pictures.observations: Actually inspected the complete recent panorama. Large tufa courses survive inside the museum beneath white modern walls, with an uneven stepped top, lower broad masonry and independent displayed stone fragments. The modern upper wall/door at the left, glass partitions, railings, lights and displayed column drum are not assumed to be ancient temple fabric. The approximate camera geotag is 41°53′33″N,12°28′56″E; it is a camera position, not an ancient footprint, facing or floor elevation.

ordinaryContext.observations: Museum description confirms surviving foundation/podium walling lies mostly beneath Palazzo Caffarelli. No bespoke architectural survey or archival reconstruction was pursued.
